name: Yahadian
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Berry, Keith & Christine Berry 1987. A survey of the South Bird's Head Stock (SIL; phonology or text collection Glottolog's most extensive description for Yahadian). Not retrievable online (sil.org search 403).

sources.citation: Mayor, Infak Insaswar & Yusuf Willem Sawaki. 2025. Exploring alienable-inalienable possessions in Yaben. Linguistik Indonesia 43(2): 205-223.
sources.note: Yaben = Konda [knd, kond1303], the sister language (authors: 61% lexical similarity with Yahadian), not Yahadian; possession only; nothing on stress. Recorded to settle the Yaben/Yabin name question.

sources.citation: Holton, Gary & Marian Klamer. 2018. The Papuan languages of East Nusantara and the Bird's Head. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area, 569-640. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Yahadian appears only in the language table (source = de Vries 2004) and in morphosyntactic remarks; the stress paragraph (p.587) discusses Moskona, Western Pantar, Inanwatan and TAP languages, nothing on Yahadian.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2004. A short grammar of Inanwatan: an endangered language of the Bird's Head of Papua, Indonesia. Pacific Linguistics 560. Canberra: ANU. Appendix 3, sec. 3 'The Yahadian language', pp. 143-150 (Mugim dialect).
sources.note: No prose statement on Yahadian stress. Sec. 3.1 (p.144) gives a phone inventory (21 C, 8 V) and one phonotactic sentence ('Yahadian allows CC clusters and at least some word-final C'). The 209-item Mugim word list (pp.144-147) marks primary stress with a tick on each item; marks fall on initial and non-initial syllables in roughly equal numbers (rough tally of text: 91 initial vs 89 non-initial of 180 marked tokens; e.g. 'dEpE ear vs dE'rE hand, di'nam tooth, hE'dE water, pacu'ar fog). Kin-term plurals in -o printed with accent on the suffix (p.150). The 'unpredictable, lexical word stress' s…

sources.citation: Berry, Keith & Christine Berry. 1987. A survey of the South Bird's Head Stock. Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 4: 81-117. (Yahadian sec. 4.1.2 p.92; Phonological features sec. 3.3 p.89; Mugim word list in Appendix C pp.99-117.)
sources.note: Silent on stress. Sec. 3.3 covers only phonotactics for the stock as a whole ('generally do not allow word final consonants.. simple VCV or CVCV syllabic structure'; Yahadian example ~remei 'shy'). Appendix C word lists carry no stress marks. This is the source the earlier scan named as unreachable; it was already held under and is now hard-linked into the yaha1248 folder.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Entry 56 Yahadian, p.34; 40-item list no. 56.
sources.note: Classification, villages (Yahadian, Mugim), source list (Cowan 1953 GN, 1958a, 1960, 1963, 1965b; Galis 1955) and a 40-word list without stress marks. Silent.

sources.citation: Cowan, H. K. J. 1960. Nadere gegevens betreffende de verbreiding der West-Papoease taalgroep (Vogelkop, Nieuw-Guinea). Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 116(3): 350-364. doi:10.1163/22134379-90002210
sources.note: Comparative lexical notes; Jahadian forms cited passim; nothing on accent/klemtoon. Silent.

sources.citation: Cowan, H. K. J. 1957. Prospects of a 'Papuan' comparative linguistics. BKI 113(1): 70-91.
sources.note: Does not treat Jahadian at all (NW Vogelkop and North Halmahera); discarded, not.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. 'Yahadian'. NewGuineaWorld (DokuWiki, UZH host), families/trans-new-guinea/berau-gulf/north-berau-gulf/yabin/yahadian.
sources.note: Second-hand compilation from de Vries 2004; phonology section '[under construction]' with the inventory only. Sole prosodic remark: the kin-term plural suffix /-o/ 'is typically stressed (de Vries 2004: 149-150)'. No word-stress rule.

sources.citation: Smits, Leo & C. L. Voorhoeve (eds.). 1998. The J. C. Anceaux collection of wordlists of Irian Jaya, B: Non-Austronesian (Papuan) languages, Part II (Irian Jaya Source Materials 10). Leiden/Jakarta: DSALCUL/IRIS. 250 pp.

sources.note: Fuller Yahadian/Mugim and Konda wordlists from Anceaux's 1950s fieldwork; his transcriptions often mark stress, which would give a second independent stress-marked list to compare with de Vries 2004. No prose rule expected.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 1995 field notes and recordings, Mugim (26-27 Sept 1995) and Yahadian-village informant (Inanwatan, Oct 1995), underlying PL-560 Appendix 3.

sources.note: The stress ticks in the published list come from these notes; any unpublished remark on Yahadian accent would be here (VU Amsterdam; not known to be archived).

sources.citation: Cowan, H. K. J. 1957. Een tweede grote Papoea-taalgroepering in Nederlands-Nieuw-Guinea. Nieuw-Guinea Studien 1: 106-118; and Cowan, H. K. J. 1958. A large Papuan language phylum in West New Guinea. Oceania 28(2): 159-166.

sources.note: Cowan's comparative treatment of Konda/Jahadian/Kampong Baru/Puragi with phonemic-system summaries; low chance of an accent remark but they are the remaining Cowan items Voorhoeve lists for Yahadian.
